# Overview

The citation analysis apparatus has five core processes, supported by a shared
infrastructure of normalisation, deduplication, and metadata management. This
document explains how each component works and how they interact.

# Module Map

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `detector.py` | Multi-method citation detection (5 methods applied per paper) |
| `resolver.py` | Resolves unmatched citations via LLM inference from contexts |
| `graph.py` | Builds multi-generational citation graph with deduplication |
| `tei_parser.py` | Parses GROBID's TEI-XML; splits compound references |
| `grobid_client.py` | HTTP client for GROBID; OCR fallback for scanned PDFs |
| `normalize.py` | Per-entry normalisation applied at graph construction time |
| `enricher.py` | CrossRef enrichment — additive metadata, never identification |
| `postprocess.py` | LLM cleaning passes run after enrichment (entry types, near-dups, compound splitting) |
| `audit.py` | Stratified random sampling and flag annotation for manual validation |
| `exporter.py` | Graph export to GraphML, GEXF, and CSV formats |
| `context_extractor.py` | Extracts verbatim citation contexts *(tabled)* |
| `llm_analyzer.py` | Citation function classification and cluster characterization *(tabled)* |
| `cluster_analyzer.py` | Co-occurrence matrix and cluster detection *(tabled)* |
| `coverage.py` | PDF coverage reporting and OA acquisition planning |
| `metadata.py` | Controlled vocabularies and output metadata |
| `zotero_csv.py` | Zotero CSV import for exact PDF↔citekey matching |
| `biblatex_model.py` | Biblatex data model and completeness scoring |
| `utils.py` | Config, citekey generation, I/O, signal handling |

# Citation Detection: The Five Methods

For each paper in the corpus, five detection methods are applied independently.
Their results are merged and deduplicated into a single set of citations. Each
citation is tagged with which methods found it (provenance tracking).

## Method 1: GROBID Bibliography

GROBID's ML models parse the PDF's reference list into structured `<biblStruct>`
entries. The TEI parser post-processes these to split compound references
(dash-abbreviated authors) and detect merged entries. This yields the richest
metadata (title, journal, volume, pages, DOI) when it works.

**Strengths**: Rich structured metadata. DOIs when available.

**Weaknesses**: Trained on STEM articles. Misses footnote-style references.
Fails on non-standard layouts. Under-counts when reference lists use humanities
conventions.

## Method 2: GROBID Inline Markers

GROBID annotates `<ref type="bibr">` elements in the body text. (Author, year)
pairs are extracted from the marker text independently of whether the
corresponding bibliography entry was successfully parsed.

**Strengths**: ML-detected, handles diverse inline styles.

**Weaknesses**: Only catches citations GROBID recognized as references.

## Method 3: Regex Patterns

Pattern matching for standard citation forms in the raw body text: parenthetical
`(Smith 2020)`, narrative `Smith (2020)`, multi-author, et al., semicolon-
separated groups. Handles non-English connectors (og, und, och, et).

**Strengths**: Fast. Catches formally styled citations GROBID missed.

**Weaknesses**: Cannot detect discursive references or organizational authors.
Unreliable for multilingual text.

## Method 4: LLM Body Scan

Each paragraph is sent to the local LLM with a prompt asking it to identify all
referenced works. This catches discursive references, organisational authors,
and any citation style recognisable to the LLM.

**Strengths**: Most comprehensive detection. Handles any citation style.

**Weaknesses**: Slowest method by a large margin. May produce false positives.

## Method 5: LLM Footnote Extraction

Each footnote containing year patterns is sent to the LLM with a structured
extraction prompt. The LLM returns full bibliographic metadata — not just
(author, year) but title, journal, volume, pages, entry type. Essential for
papers using Chicago footnote style.

**Strengths**: Extracts rich metadata from footnote prose. Handles multiple
references per footnote.

**Weaknesses**: Depends on LLM accuracy.

## Merging

After all five methods run, results are merged by normalized (author, year) key.
When multiple methods detect the same citation, their provenance tags are
combined. The merged set represents our best knowledge of every work cited
anywhere in the document.

# OCR Fallback

Some PDFs have no embedded text layer. GROBID returns HTTP 500 with
`[NO_BLOCKS]` for these. `grobid_client.py` detects this signal, runs
`ocrmypdf` to add a text layer, backs up the original to `output/ocr/originals/`,
replaces the PDF in place, and retries GROBID. The backup's presence is the
cache signal on subsequent runs.

# Resolution

For citations detected in the text but not matched to any existing bibliography
entry, the resolver uses only the LLM. CrossRef is not used for resolution —
author+year queries to CrossRef produce a high rate of false positives because
CrossRef always returns a result regardless of domain. See
`docs/methods/resolver-method.md` for the full rationale.

The LLM receives up to three citation contexts (paragraphs where the citation
appears) and infers full bibliographic metadata: title, journal, entry type,
co-authors. If no contexts are available, the entry becomes a stub preserving
the citation relationship without metadata. Stubs may be resolved naturally on
subsequent papers where the work appears as a complete GROBID bibliography entry.

Resolved entries are tagged with `_resolution_method` (llm_from_context,
llm_from_footnote, stub) and `_resolution_confidence` (medium, low).

# Graph Construction

The citation graph is built incrementally:

1. **Seed paper**: Extract all citations (5 methods). Add to bibliography as F1.
2. **F1 papers**: For each PDF, extract all citations (5 methods). Match the
   paper to its existing F1 entry. Add its citations as F2.
3. **Deduplication**: Each new entry is checked against existing entries by four
   strategies in order: DOI, exact title, author+year+fuzzy title, and
   cross-script transliteration (Cyrillic ↔ Latin via ALA-LC table). Duplicates
   are merged, accumulating cited_by links.
4. **Per-paper enrichment**: Each newly added entry is enriched via CrossRef
   immediately after insertion, so its title is available for deduplication of
   subsequent papers.

Matching an F1 PDF to its bibliography entry uses a tiered strategy: Zotero CSV
(if provided) → DOI → exact title → author+year.

# Normalisation

Normalisation runs per-entry at creation time inside `normalize_entry()` in
`normalize.py`. Every new entry is normalised before being added to the
bibliography:

- **Title cleanup**: ALL-CAPS conversion, letter prefix stripping (`"a: Title"`
  → `"Title"`), hyphenated line-break joining, LLM placeholder title removal,
  oversized title flagging (`_title_too_long` for titles >300 chars)
- **Field normalisation**: DOI prefix stripping, date-to-year extraction, page
  range normalisation, volume extraction from pages field
- **Entry type**: Conservative reclassification for `misc` entries only, based
  on available fields

Corpus-wide author given-name normalisation (preferring the most complete form
seen for each family name) runs at save time.

# Enrichment

After the full corpus is processed, `--enrich` fills in missing metadata fields
from CrossRef. Two strategies: DOI lookup (fully reliable) and title query
(accepted only at ≥0.85 title similarity). Enrichment is strictly additive —
existing fields are never overwritten, and entry identity (citekey, generation,
cited_by) is never changed. See `docs/methods/resolver-method.md`.

# Post-processing

`--postprocess` runs LLM cleaning passes after enrichment, on fields that are
best assessed once the full enriched bibliography is available:

- **Entry type reclassification**: uses enriched `journaltitle`, `volume`,
  `pages`, and `editor` fields to correct types set under incomplete data, with
  guards against false reclassification (monograph series ≠ journals,
  incollection not demoted to inbook)
- **Near-duplicate resolution**: LLM asked "are these the same work?" for
  title-rich entry pairs with ≥70% token overlap; trivial titles (Introduction,
  Conclusion, etc.) are excluded; unresolved pairs are flagged for audit
- **Compound citation splitting**: LLM splits `_raw_citation` strings for
  entries flagged as possibly compound

# Completeness Scoring

Each bibliography entry receives a `completeness` field with a score (0.0–1.0)
and a breakdown of which fields are present vs. expected for its entry type.
Used by the audit tool to stratify entries for manual review.

# Audit

`--audit` draws a stratified random sample from the bibliography for human
review and annotates the full bibliography with data quality flags:

**Sample strata**: CrossRef-resolved, unresolved, minimal-completeness, suspected
duplicate pairs, OCR-source entries, non-English source papers per language.

**Flag strata**: citekey suffix collisions, oversized titles (`_title_too_long`),
missing given names, near-duplicate candidates (`_near_duplicate_candidate`).

Output is `output/audit_sample.md`, designed for direct annotation. See
`docs/methods/audit-sampling.md` for full methodological documentation.

# Export

`--export` produces four output files via `exporter.py`:

- `citation_graph.graphml` — for R/igraph (reads natively, direction preserved)
- `citation_graph.gexf` — for Gephi
- `citation_edgelist.csv` — directed source→target pairs
- `citation_nodes.csv` — node attributes: title, year, generation, entry_type,
  first_author, doi, completeness, in/out degree

# Graceful Cancellation

Ctrl-C during a long-running stage writes the current bibliography state to
`_partial_bibliography.json` before exiting, preventing loss of work during
multi-hour LLM runs.

# CLI Flags

| Flag | Stage | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | 1-4 | Run full pipeline |
| `--extract` | 1 | Seed paper only |
| `--iterate-f1` | 2 | F1 papers → citation graph |
| `--enrich` | 3 | CrossRef enrichment of bibliography |
| `--enrich-bib-only` | 3 | Bibliography enrichment only |
| `--enrich-auth-only` | 3 | Author enrichment only |
| `--postprocess` | 4 | LLM cleaning passes (post-enrich) |
| `--audit` | 5 | Draw stratified audit sample + flag annotations |
| `--export` | 6 | Export graph to GraphML, GEXF, CSV |
| `--coverage` | — | PDF coverage report + OA lookup |
| `--audit-n N` | — | Entries per audit stratum (default: 10) |
| `--audit-seed N` | — | Random seed for audit sampling (default: 42) |
| `--audit-threshold F` | — | Duplicate similarity threshold (default: 0.85) |
| `--limit N` | 2 | Process only N F1 papers |
| `--email` | 2,3 | Contact email for CrossRef polite pool |
| `--model` | 2,4 | Override LLM model name |
| `--verbose` | all | Debug logging |
